All-New Axiom Grit 3814 Fifth Wheel Toy Hauler Delivers a Premium Experience at a Smaller Price
40 photos
Photo: Axiom RV
Exactly one year ago, a new name exploded on the RV market with a pair of products that defied all expectations regarding fifth wheelers: Axiom RV. One year after this stellar debut, Axiom is hard at work to build on it, adding to those initial two series more budget-friendly variants.
Axiom's debut included the Vendetta fifth wheel toy hauler and the Imperium luxury fifth wheel RV, each with a couple of more floorplans to choose from and several options you could add to get an even nicer experience. For 2027, each of these series is getting a price-conscious alternative: Imperium with the Avora and Vendetta with the Grit.
Both Avora and Grit will be standalone series with four floorplans in between them, two for each, and both made their debut last month (September) at a U.S. trade event. Today's focus is Grit, the Grit 3814 specifically, which is a family-friendly toy hauler with all the features Axiom has come to be famous for but a lower price tag than the Vendetta it's inspired by.
Since this is still a pre-production floorplan, it's not even featured on the official Axiom page yet among the available products. But Grit 3814 does get a landing page, official photos, and minimum specs, as well as a nice introductory walkthrough video you will find at the bottom of the page. In short, we have all we need to get a nice appreciation of an upcoming product in all its (oversize) glory.
Photo: Axiom RV First off, Axiom is keen to underline that, despite the price-conscious angle to the Grit toy hauler, it's still an Axiom product getting the Axiom staple features that drew international attention last year. That means all-steel construction, extra tall ceilings, extra tall slide-outs with flush floor, residential finishes and appliances, residential mini-split system for HVAC, and a generator moved behind the axle, under the chassis, for the largest pass-through storage compartment of the entire class.
This might be a more "budget" product, but make no mistake about it, it's still top of its class, still premium in every way that counts. It's like the Vendetta before it but with some costs shaved off here and there.
The Grit 3814 is the first of the planned line, a triple-axle three-slide widebody toy hauler that's equally suitable for hauling toys as it's to accommodate the entire family. It's different from its more higher-end predecessors by its gray and white paintjob, which it shares with the Avora. Suspension is a downgraded Curt leaf spring suspension instead of TCS independent suspension, with Solera legged awnings instead of Gerard armless ones.
Photo: Axiom RV The Pathfinder lighting system is still present, as you'd expect, since it sets Axiom RVs apart from all the other big boys and girls out there. This unit comes in at 43 feet 10 inches (13.3 meters) in length, 14 feet (4.2 meters) of which are dedicated to the garage space, and 13 feet 5 inches (4 meters) of height.
The Grit 3814 is a front bedroom floorplan with Axiom-standard picture windows, all of them Euro square, frameless ones, premium custom cabinetry with soft-close hinges, dovetail joinery, and adjustable shelves, and residential appliances.
The main entrance is in one of the campsite slide-outs, directly into the open-plan kitchen and living space. This allows Axiom to put an expandable standalone dinette by the door, with a full fridge and pantry on the other side. This also allows Axiom to offer full access to the fridge with the slide closed, which apparently was a very requested customer demand.
Photo: Axiom RV In front of the entrance is the living room , with a gorgeous L-shaped sectional with integrated recliners and an entertainment center with a 55-inch smart TV, an electric fireplace, and a JBL portable speaker. Storage is integrated throughout, wherever possible, which is great considering this is meant as a family-friendly solution even for extended stays.
The kitchen is a horseshoe-shaped unit with the kitchen peninsula sliding in and out of the main kitchen block with the corresponding slide-out. It might seem a compact kitchen but it's very nicely appointed, from the all-accessory sink to the four-burner cooktop and the large microwave, and storage and prep space galore.
Another customer demand integrated into this Grit floorplan is the addition of an entrance to the garage loft from the kitchen space. Basically, you can use the same ladder you use in the garage to get to the loft, but from the kitchen side.
Photo: Axiom RV Speaking of the garage, it's the highlight of the floorplan . It's designed for toys, even larger side-by-sides, but it can also double as a secondary bedroom with its separate bathroom facilities and entertainment. A split collapsible bathroom, a mini-split, a TV, and a combination of a HappiJac sofa and drop-down double bed are all included in the standard package.
At the front of the trailer is the bathroom and main bedroom, in typical fifth wheel fashion. In the bathroom, you'll find a one-piece fiberglass shower with a rain head, a porcelain toilet, and a small sink on a slimline vanity that integrates some storage.
The bedroom comes with a king bed in a slide-out, a dresser, and a full wardrobe in the front cap. Axiom erases the large windshield in that front cap to offer more storage, also based on customer requests, and the result is a wardrobe with hanging space and a separate closet with washer-dryer prep.
Photo: Axiom RV The Grit 3814 comes standard with Victron energy power system and 400W of solar on the roof, upgradable to as much as 3200W through the AX Boondocker series packages, six-point hydraulic leveling, Fogatti on-demand water heater, and Starlink prep. Dry weight is 16,500 lbs (7,484 kg), with a reported gross weight of 24,000 lbs (10,886 kg).
Axiom says this fifth wheel toy hauler is designed for "travelers who demand maximum space in a manageable footprint without compromising," and that will mean a price tag worthy of the "uncompromising" descriptor. MSRP will be at around $193,000 before options. It's cost-conscious only in relation to the Axiom Vendetta, which is about $50K more expensive in base configuration.
